question_stem:
Two cyclists, Isabella and Maria, are having a race. They both travel along a straight road with constant acceleration, starting from rest at point $A$.

Isabella accelerates for $5 \text{ s}$ at a constant rate $a \text{ m s}^{-2}$. She then travels at the constant speed she has reached for $10 \text{ s}$, before decelerating to rest at a constant rate over a period of $5 \text{ s}$.

Maria accelerates at a constant rate, reaching a speed of $5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ in a distance of $27.5 \text{ m}$. She then maintains this speed for a period of $10 \text{ s}$, before decelerating to rest at a constant rate over a period of $5 \text{ s}$.
context_texts: Maria travels further: Isabella $82.5$ m; Maria $90$ m.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question_text: Given that $a = 1.1$, find which cyclist travels further.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text: Find the value of $a$ for which the two cyclists travel the same distance.
